facts: Sam Bankman-Fried was convicted of seven criminal charges including wire fraud, conspiracy, and money laundering.
On March 28, 2024, Bankman-Fried was sentenced to 25 years in prison and ordered to forfeit $11 billion.
Bankman-Fried co-founded the cryptocurrency exchange FTX and the quantitative trading firm Alameda Research.
He graduated from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 2014 with a bachelor's degree in physics and a minor in mathematics.
By April 2023, $7.3 billion of the original $8 billion in missing funds had been recuperated in liquid assets.
In September 2021, Bankman-Fried and the senior staff of FTX moved from Hong Kong to the Bahamas.
